teacher: large hosted generative model acting as teacher inside the coding session
induced_from: train-split failures of run s15-base only; validation and test failures were never shown to the teacher

misread_or_logic.why: The code contradicts the visible example or uses a wrong algorithm; a short rule cannot supply the algorithm, but running the example exposes the contradiction.

knowledge_gap.fixable_by_prompt_rule: yes, if the bank holds the definition
knowledge_gap.why: The student does not know a named sequence or formula; feedback cannot conjure it, a retrieved definition can.

careless_code_error.why: Undefined names, bad calls and syntax slips produce a precise error message when the example is run.

name_mismatch.why: The function is named differently from the example call; an alias repairs it without any model call.

hidden_wrong_output_spec.why: The statement is ambiguous and the hidden tests encode one convention (re.search, None on no match, split(' ')).

hidden_crash_edge.why: Crash on empty or negative input that the visible example does not exercise.

reference_quirk.why: The reference solution behaves unexpectedly; no sensible rule predicts it.

missing_base_or_empty_case.why: Recursion without a base case or max() of an empty container.

hardcoded_from_example.why: A size or exponent was copied from the single example instead of computed.

hidden_wrong_output_edge.why: Bit trick breaks for negative operands.

efficiency.why: Linear divisor loop times out for n near 10**9.

observations: Random-subset run on train: 107/182 solved vs 115/182 without rules (7 fixed, 15 broken).
Mean change by number of rules shown: 1 rule +0.06, 2 rules -0.06, 3 rules -0.04, 4 rules -0.14.
Sample code inside a rule is copied literally (`return []`, `return 0`), also where it is wrong.
A rule that bundles several definitions gets them mixed up; a single definition shown alone was applied.
rounds.decision: Retire every always-on and broad rule; keep only narrow triggers; one concept per knowledge rule; show at most 2 rules.

rounds.criterion: on development tasks where a rule fires, fixed >= broken
rounds.decision: criterion met; bank frozen before the single test evaluation

rules.text: The n-th triangular number is n*(n+1)//2.
The n-th pentagonal number is n*(3*n-1)//2.
The n-th hexagonal number is n*(2*n-1).
The n-th heptagonal number is n*(5*n-3)//2.
The n-th octagonal number is n*(3*n-2).
The n-th nonagonal number is n*(7*n-5)//2.
The n-th decagonal number is n*(4*n-3).
The n-th dodecagonal number is n*(5*n-4).
The n-th centered triangular number is 3*n*(n-1)//2 + 1.
The n-th centered square number is 2*n*(n-1) + 1.
The n-th centered pentagonal number is 5*n*(n-1)//2 + 1.
The n-th centered hexagonal number is 3*n*(n-1) + 1.
The n-th star number is 6*n*(n-1) + 1.
The n-th tetrahedral number is n*(n+1)*(n+2)//6.
The n-th square pyramidal number is n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)//6.
The n-th octahedral number is n*(2*n*n+1)//3.
Woodall numbers are k*2**k - 1 for k = 1, 2, 3, ... (1, 7, 23, 63, 159, 383). To test a number, loop k upward and compare k*2**k - 1 with it until the term exceeds it.
Cullen numbers are k*2**k + 1 for k = 0, 1, 2, ... (1, 3, 9, 25, 65).
Mersenne numbers are 2**k - 1 (1, 3, 7, 15, 31).
The n-th Carol number is (2**n - 1)**2 - 2 (-1, 7, 47, 223).
The n-th Kynea number is (2**n + 1)**2 - 2 (7, 23, 79, 287).
Lucas numbers: L(0)=2, L(1)=1, L(n)=L(n-1)+L(n-2).
Pell numbers: P(0)=0, P(1)=1, P(n)=2*P(n-1)+P(n-2).
Jacobsthal-Lucas numbers: j(0)=2, j(1)=1, j(n)=j(n-1)+2*j(n-2) (2, 1, 5, 7, 17, 31).
Perrin numbers: P(0)=3, P(1)=0, P(2)=2, P(n)=P(n-2)+P(n-3).
Padovan numbers: P(0)=P(1)=P(2)=1, P(n)=P(n-2)+P(n-3).
Newman-Conway sequence: P(1)=P(2)=1 and P(n)=P(P(n-1))+P(n-P(n-1)). Fill a list bottom-up from index 1.
Newman-Shanks-Williams numbers: S(0)=1, S(1)=1, S(n)=2*S(n-1)+S(n-2) (1, 1, 3, 7, 17, 41); the n-th one is S(n).
The n-th Catalan number is math.comb(2*n, n)//(n+1) (1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42).
Bell numbers (1, 1, 2, 5, 15, 52): build the Bell triangle; each row starts with the last value of the previous row and each next entry adds the entry above-left.
Stirling numbers of the second kind: S(n,k)=k*S(n-1,k)+S(n-1,k-1), S(0,0)=1, S(n,0)=0 for n>0.
Eulerian number: A(n,m)=(n-m)*A(n-1,m-1)+(m+1)*A(n-1,m), with A(n,0)=1 and A(n,m)=0 when m>=n.
Delannoy number: D(m,n)=D(m-1,n)+D(m-1,n-1)+D(m,n-1), with D(0,n)=D(m,0)=1.
The sum of the even-index binomial coefficients C(n,0)+C(n,2)+... equals 2**(n-1).
The sum of products of consecutive binomial coefficients, C(n,k)*C(n,k+1) over k, equals math.comb(2*n, n-1).
Armstrong number: with k = number of digits, sum(d**k for each digit d) == n. The power is k, not always 3.
Amicable numbers: let d(x) be the sum of divisors of x smaller than x. a is amicable when b = d(a) differs from a and d(b) == a. Sum every such a in the range.
Perfect number: the sum of its divisors smaller than n equals n (6, 28, 496).
Abundant number: the sum of divisors smaller than n is greater than n; deficient: it is less than n.
Harshad (Niven) number: n % (sum of its digits) == 0.
Strong number: the sum of the factorials of its digits equals n (145 = 1! + 4! + 5!).
Automorphic number: str(n*n) ends with str(n).
Cylinder (math.pi): lateral surface 2*pi*r*h, total surface 2*pi*r*(r+h), volume pi*r*r*h.
Cone (math.pi): slant l = sqrt(r*r+h*h), lateral surface pi*r*l, total surface pi*r*(r+l), volume pi*r*r*h/3.
Sphere (math.pi): surface 4*pi*r*r, volume 4/3*pi*r**3.
Cube with side a: total surface 6*a*a, lateral surface 4*a*a, volume a**3.
Cuboid l, w, h: total surface 2*(l*w+l*h+w*h), lateral surface 2*h*(l+w), volume l*w*h.
Square pyramid with base edge b and slant height s: surface b*b + 2*b*s; volume with vertical height h: b*b*h/3.
Regular tetrahedron with edge a: surface sqrt(3)*a*a, volume a**3/(6*sqrt(2)).
Trapezium with parallel sides a, b and height h: area (a+b)/2*h, median (a+b)/2.
Rhombus: area p*q/2 from diagonals p, q; perimeter 4*side.
Circular sector with angle in degrees: area math.pi*r*r*angle/360.
Arc length with angle in degrees: 2*math.pi*r*angle/360.
Regular polygon with n sides of length s: area n*s*s/(4*math.tan(math.pi/n)).

trigger.pattern: differ\w* at one bit|one bit position

rules.text: Two numbers differ in exactly one bit when x = a ^ b satisfies `x > 0 and x & (x - 1) == 0`.
Polygonal numbers, n-th term: triangular n*(n+1)//2, pentagonal n*(3*n-1)//2, hexagonal n*(2*n-1), heptagonal n*(5*n-3)//2, octagonal n*(3*n-2), nonagonal n*(7*n-5)//2, decagonal n*(4*n-3).

rules.text: Woodall numbers are n*2**n - 1 (1, 7, 23, 63, 159, 383, ...); Cullen n*2**n + 1; Mersenne 2**n - 1; Carol (2**n - 1)**2 - 2; Kynea (2**n + 1)**2 - 2. To test membership, generate terms in a loop until they reach the input.

rules.text: Catalan C(n)=math.comb(2*n, n)//(n+1). Bell numbers: build the Bell triangle, each row starting with the last value of the previous row. Stirling (second kind) S(n,k)=k*S(n-1,k)+S(n-1,k-1). Eulerian A(n,m)=(n-m)*A(n-1,m-1)+(m+1)*A(n-1,m) with A(n,0)=1 and A(n,m)=0 for m>=n. Delannoy D(m,n)=D(m-1,n)+D(m-1,n-1)+D(m,n-1).

rules.text: Binomial sums: all C(n,k) add to 2**n; even-index terms add to 2**(n-1), odd-index terms too; sum of C(n,k)**2 is C(2n,n); sum of C(n,k)*C(n,k+1) is C(2n,n-1). Use math.comb.
rules.retire_reason: split into one rule per identity

rules.text: Armstrong number: sum(d**k for each digit d) == n where k is the number of digits (not always 3). Proper divisors exclude the number itself. Perfect: sum of proper divisors == n. Amicable pair: a != b, sumdiv(a) == b and sumdiv(b) == a. Harshad: n % digit_sum == 0.
rules.retire_reason: split; the student mixed up two definitions from the same rule (digit sum used as divisor sum)

Sphere area 4*pi*r*r, volume 4/3*pi*r**3. Cube 6*a*a, lateral 4*a*a. Cuboid 2*(l*w+l*h+w*h), lateral 2*h*(l+w). Square pyramid b*b+2*b*slant. Tetrahedron area sqrt(3)*a*a.

rules.text: Wind chill index (v in km/h, t in Celsius): 13.12 + 0.6215*t - 11.37*v**0.16 + 0.3965*t*v**0.16, then round as the task says.
Months with 31 days: 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. Months with 30 days: 4, 6, 9, 11. February (2) has 28 or 29 days and belongs to neither group.

Bit idioms: exactly one bit set (power of two, or two numbers differ in one bit via x = a ^ b) is `x > 0 and x & (x - 1) == 0`; lowest set bit `x & -x`; set bit i `x | (1 << i)`; clear `x & ~(1 << i)`; toggle `x ^ (1 << i)`; highest bit position `x.bit_length() - 1`; `bin(x).count('1')` only for x >= 0.
rules.retire_reason: replaced by a single idiom for the one failure it explained

rules.text: Define the function with exactly the name used in the example assert, copied character for character, even if it looks misspelled or is a built-in name.
rules.retire_reason: always-on; 2 wins vs 10 losses when included; the alias codemod fixes the same failure with no model call

rules.text: Handle empty input first, e.g. `if not items: return []` (or `0`, `''` as fits). Never index `[0]`, take `% len(x)`, or call `max()`/`min()` without `default=` on something that may be empty.
rules.retire_reason: fired on 67% of tasks; lasso -0.12; its sample `return []` was copied literally where the right empty value was () or 0 or a size

rules.text: Inputs may be negative or zero: use `abs(n)` before a `str(n)` digit loop.
For text-pattern tasks use `re.search`, which finds the pattern anywhere in the string, not `re.match`, unless the task says the string must start with the pattern.
When nothing is found, return `None` itself, not a tuple or list filled with None; return a finished value, never a generator (`yield`).
rules.retire_reason: trigger matched unrelated 'occurrence' tasks; 1 win vs 1 loss

rules.text: The input mixes strings and numbers: keep only the numbers first, `nums = [x for x in items if isinstance(x, int)]`, then compute on `nums`.
Give every recursion a base case that stops at 0 (`if n <= 0: return 0` or the right start value) and cache it with `@functools.lru_cache(None)`; prefer a loop that fills a list for sequences.
rules.retire_reason: its sample base case `return 0` overwrote correct start values (Newman-Shanks-Williams got S(0)=0)

rules.text: Split on the exact character the task names, e.g. `s.split(' ')`; bare `split()` merges whitespace and drops empty strings.
Loop divisors only up to `int(n ** 0.5)`: when `i` divides `n` count both `i` and `n // i` (once if equal). Inputs can be near 10**9, so an O(n) loop is too slow.
rules.retire_reason: 2 inclusions, 2 losses

rules.text: Return the same type and shape as the expected value in the example: a tuple stays a tuple, nested lists stay nested, a converted string is returned as a string (not True/False).
rules.retire_reason: always-on; 4 wins vs 9 losses; over-applied (answers wrapped in tuples or lists that the task did not ask for)

rules.text: Never hard-code a size, exponent or count taken from the example (such as 4 rows or power 3); compute it from the input with `len(...)`.
rules.retire_reason: always-on; contrast 0.00; no measurable benefit for the prompt space it uses

rules.text: Begin the code with a comment `# example:` stating in one line how the example input becomes the example output; the function must return exactly that value for that input.
rules.retire_reason: always-on; 2 wins vs 7 losses; the comment did not change how the student read the example

codemods.name: alias_entry_point
codemods.what: If the function called in the example is not defined, bind that name to the single (or closest-named) function the answer defines.

codemods.name: add_missing_imports
codemods.what: Prepend imports for standard-library modules and well-known helpers that are used but never imported.
